County Minimum-Wage Panel Used in the Study

Source: R/input.R
minimum_wage.Rd

The study's seven-year balanced county panel, with convenience aliases for the outcome, absorbing treatment, county identifier, and state identifier. Original study variables are retained without alteration.

Usage

data(minimum_wage)

Format

A data frame with 15,988 rows and 28 columns:

id, countyreal, FIPS

Numeric county identifiers.

year

Calendar year, from 2001 through 2007.

Y, lemp

Log employment, the study outcome.

D

Absorbing treatment indicator: one from the first treatment year.

state

Numeric state FIPS identifier, usable for state clustering.

cohort, first.treat

First treatment calendar year; zero for never treated.

state_name, county_name

State and county names.

emp0A01_BS

Employment count underlying the log outcome.

quarter

Quarter of the underlying observation.

censusdiv, region

Census division and region factors.

msa

Indicator for metropolitan statistical area status.

pop, lpop

Population measure and its natural logarithm.

white, black

White and Black population shares in the study input.

hs, col

High-school and college attainment measures.

medinc, lmedinc

Median income measure and its natural logarithm.

pov

Poverty measure.

nssi

Study input's nssi demographic variable.

treat

Indicator for ever belonging to a treated cohort; this is not D.

Source

County panel of the minimum-wage application in Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021), "Difference-in-Differences with Multiple Time Periods", Journal of Econometrics, 225(2), 200–230, as used in Liu (2026), "Cohort-Anchored HonestDiD" (arXiv:2509.01829). The script data-raw/prepare-minimum-wage.R in the package's source repository records all convenience aliases.
